A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms and experiments. Their text, equations, algorithm boxes, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 Section 6 and Figure 1 report original simulations comparing four algorithms on synthetic tabular MDPs.

after.justification: V2 Section 5 and Appendix B retain these original simulations and their regret curves.

M1.justification: ULCB-Hoeffding and Refined AMB retain their action selection, updates, bonuses and truncation rules. Explicit counter bookkeeping and a corrected learning-rate index clarify the pseudocode without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic episodic tabular MDPs at four scales: (H,S,A) = (2,3,3), (5,5,5), (7,8,6) and (10,15,10). No additional dataset, task or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: All four experiments retain AMB, Refined AMB, UCB-Hoeffding and ULCB-Hoeffding. The added model-based comparisons in Appendix C concern theoretical guarantees, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reward and transition generation, initial-state sampling, episode budgets, Regret(T)/log(K+1), and bonus settings are unchanged. Both use iota = 1 and bonus coefficients 1 for the three alternatives and 2 for AMB.

E4.justification: Neither version reports additional experimental ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness studies or case studies. V2's new appendices supply theoretical comparisons and proofs; Appendix B redisplays the existing experiments.

E5.justification: Both report 10 sample trajectories per algorithm under the same MDP instance, median curves and 10th–90th percentile bands. No run-count, seed or statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The four Figure 1 plot images are identical across versions. Both retain the finding that UCB-Hoeffding performs best overall, while ULCB-Hoeffding and Refined AMB perform comparably and outperform AMB.

T1.justification: V2 adds the analytical framework in Section 3.2, weight lemmas in Appendix D, and proofs of the UCB-Hoeffding and ULCB-Hoeffding guarantees in Appendices E–F, which v1 lacked. Although the main UCB bound is retained, its simplified optimal-triple term changes from H^6 to H^5. Refined AMB's stated multiple-optimal-action term likewise changes from H^6 to H^5, and new Appendix G.4 derives absorption of the additive SAH^2 term. The earlier AMB optimism proof is largely retained.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the headline priority claim from the first fine-grained bounds for model-free RL generally to the first such UCB-based bound plus rigorous non-UCB counterparts. It explicitly credits AMB with the earlier fine-grained bound while retaining the same substantive algorithmic contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses horizon dependence versus state-space and memory costs, explains the historical-versus-current value-estimate mismatch that obstructs transferring model-based analyses, and suggests possible extensions. Section 3.1 also revises the ideal-case illustration to an MDP with only one suboptimal triple at the final step. Empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 explicitly preserve visit counts for unvisited pairs, and Algorithm 2 corrects its lower-bound learning-rate index to t. These are limited specification improvements. The new reproducibility statement repeats the existing processor, 12-hour runtime and statement that code accompanies supplementary materials.

R1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands positioning against model-based research through explicit regret, memory and surplus-analysis comparisons. V2 also qualifies its novelty relative to AMB and adds Papini et al. (2021), Zhang et al. (2024a) and Zhang et al. (2026) to the linear-function-approximation discussion. Most earlier references are retained.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the main narrative around the analytical framework and two AMB refinements, rewrites the abstract and contribution summary, and moves related work to Appendix A. It adds a technical-novelty discussion and acknowledgment, ethics, reproducibility and language-model-use statements.

P2.justification: The document adopts substantially different typography, margins, title and heading styles, and denser equation and pseudocode layouts. Figure 1 is reduced and relocated from the main experiments section to Appendix B; its panels remain unchanged. Algorithm blocks are also repositioned and repacked.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is theoretical completeness and assessability: v1 states the central UCB-based guarantees without their derivations, whereas v2 supplies an explicit framework and extensive supporting analysis in Section 3.2 and Appendices D–F. The added comparison with model-based methods and more precise novelty claims further strengthen the paper. These substantially improve support for its central contribution while preserving the empirical evidence.
